Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Do not perform the task.", "input": "could you shape this into a prompt for Orson, not Nadia, to write the welcome section for the Harbor Shelf Reading Club website? the club meets online once a month, and members vote on the next book. we want new visitors to understand what the club does and feel that readers are welcome whether they read quickly or take their time. mention the monthly online discussion and the member vote, but don't make it sound like people have to finish books at a certain pace. ask for friendly, clear wording that feels natural on a website, not like an ad. keep the welcome section fairly short and focused on people who haven't visited the site before. it should invite them to join the club, but don't add details about how to sign up, what books are chosen, or when the next meeting happens, since I haven't provided those. please make the prompt clear enough for Orson to use as-is, and keep it about writing that one welcome section rather than redesigning the whole website.", "output": "Orson, not Nadia: Please write a fairly short welcome section for the Harbor Shelf Reading Club website. Use friendly, clear wording that feels natural on a website rather than like an advertisement, and focus on visitors who are new to the site. Explain that the club meets online once a month and that members vote on the next book. Help readers understand what the club does, and make clear that they are welcome whether they read quickly or take their time; don't suggest that members must finish books at a particular pace. Invite visitors to join the club, but don't add signup instructions, name any books, or give a date for the next meeting. Write only the welcome section, not a redesign of the website."}]
